title: Concept: Server header names an internal host
description: Internal hostnames follow a house naming scheme and often encode environment, region and role. Publishing one in the Server header tells the caller how the private network is named, which turns a single exposed host into a map of the estate and shortens the search for a second target.
applicability: Responses emitted by an origin or proxy that forwards its own hostname in the Server header.
risk: The caller learns the internal naming scheme and environment, which supports lateral targeting and makes internal-only hosts discoverable by name.
